messages:
emily: Heads-up — customer Acme hitting a weird streaming issue. Responses arrive as a drip (1-5B chunks) for ~10s, then a ~60–80s silence, client reconnects and gets partial JSON. Happens only on the ALB -> Cloudflare path. Trace: X-Request-ID=acme-req-9843

emily: I captured a quick repro and headers. Repro steps: curl -v -N against our /v1/streams endpoint (below).

emily: ```bash
# repro (simple)
curl -v -N "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=gptx" \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \\
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\
  --no-buffer
```

emily: Response header snapshot (from our proxy logs):
Server: envoy
Via: 1.1 cloudflare
X-Request-ID: acme-req-9843
CF-Connecting-IP: 198.51.100.22
CF-Cache-Status: DYNAMIC

emily: tcpdump (TLS frames sizes) shows lots of tiny TLS records ~30-80 bytes, then gap ~70s. Customer client sees Connection: reset after reconnect; they reported duplicate invoices for partial tokens.

jason: Thanks. Two quick Qs: 1) Is ALB set to HTTP/2 or TLS passthrough? 2) Do we see any FIN/ACK from ALB when the silence starts? Can you paste the raw edge->origin headers from logs around the stall (10s window)?

emily: ALB is fronting with HTTP/2 to the client and HTTP/1.1 to our origin. I pasted a slightly redacted log chunk: 
`[2024-09-12T15:42:10Z] edge->origin: "POST /v1/streams HTTP/1.1" 200 0ms conn_id=1234 xreq=acme-req-9843`
Then silence until ~15:43:20 when the client reconnects. No explicit 502/504.

priya: Likely two related things:
- ALB idle timeout default (60s) + http/1.1 origin connection can cause half-close behavior if the origin or runtime keeps sending tiny TLS records. ALB may flush/close and the client reconnects.
- Cloudflare can coalesce small writes and also sometimes buffer/trickle them based on heuristics. Small chunk sizes + long pauses are a classic sign.

priya: Workarounds to try quickly:
- Send heartbeat comments over SSE every 15s (e.g. `:hb\n\n`). That keeps ALB/CF state alive.
- Increase ALB idle timeout to 120–300s for the service if customers rely on long-lived streams.
- On the client side, ensure they use `curl --no-buffer` or `fetch` with `keepalive` behavior; avoid libraries that buffer until newline.

jason: Also can we enable `chunked_transfer_encoding: true` explicitly on the runtime so we flush larger frames? If runtime is emitting many tiny writes (one token per write) batching at the runtime layer would reduce coalescing pressure on proxies.

emily: We pushed a quick provocation: runtime flag `--stream-batch-ms=20` to batch micro-writes, and Acme reports the silence reduced dramatically.

emily: Customer also shared client logs — they see `ERR_HTTP2_STREAM_ERROR` after reconnect and then duplicate billing entries. Billing team flagged duplicate partial-session tokens.

rachel: We need an incident and follow-up doc. Emily/ Jason / Priya please open an INC and include: reproduction curl, tcpdump sample, headers, and the temporary mitigation (heartbeat + stream batching). Assign to eng-infra and eng-runtime for longer fix.

emily: Created INC-2345 and linked customer case CASE-9987. Added the two mitigations as hotfix: 1) runtime stream batching patch (v2.1.3-hotfix) 2) config note to recommend ALB idle >=120s for streaming routes.

deploy-bot: Deployment v2.1.3-hotfix deployed to staging at 2024-09-12T18:02:00Z.

jason: Next steps for eng-infra: get ALB idle-timeouts documented and see if we can set a per-target group override in prod for streaming endpoints. For eng-runtime: investigate smarter write coalescing (adaptive by downstream RTT).

priya: I'll take infra owner. Filed follow-up RFC: RFC-STREAM-POKE-42. Will try to reproduce with an ALB + Cloudflare test harness (scripting client with slow chunk writes). ETA EOD.

emily: Thanks all — customer on the hotfix and heartbeat workaround for now. Leaving notes in CASE-9987 and will post final findings to #postmortems when closed. :white_check_mark:
